title: Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centers: unified management of Teams apps and agents across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app
summary: Hold: the licensing field says entitlement is unpublished, but Microsoft publishes prerequisites for managing agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The briefing should give those requirements while keeping the narrower caveat that a separate licence or meter for unification itself is not published. The administration paths, commands and rollout account are supported.

claims.claim: MC796790 contains a text update dated 18 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Phase 1 for never-modified tenants began rolling out at the end of September 2025.
claims.quote: We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Phase 2 as fully rolled out.
claims.quote: This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Phase 2 makes no org-wide or app-level settings changes without administrator action.
claims.quote: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Phase 3 will automatically unify availability for tenants that have not acted.
claims.quote: Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft will announce Phase 3 timelines at least 60 days before it begins.
claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A Phase 3 start date has not yet been announced.
claims.quote: Searched: "unified app" "Phase 3" timeline. Read uam-tac-mac and supplied MC796790; the notice labels Phase 3 Future and promises a separate timeline, without giving a start date.

claims.claim: Unified app and agent installation management is generally available.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Installation unification applies to tenants whose availability has been unified.
claims.quote: Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible.

claims.claim: Installation unification completes within 24 to 48 hours after availability unification.
claims.quote: app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

claims.claim: Supported app and agent installations can be managed from either portal and synchronise across both.
claims.quote: Administrators can manage supported app and agent installations from either portal, with changes synchronized across both admin centers.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says app installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies.
claims.quote: Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Installations previously made through Teams app setup policies are not unified by this change.
claims.quote: Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

claims.claim: MC796790 associates roadmap items 393931, 485712 and 503105.
claims.quote: This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises keeping settings synchronised manually until the tenant is unified to avoid disruption.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized.

claims.claim: Microsoft's pages describe no new data access for the unification change.
claims.quote: Searched: "unified app management" data permissions approval PowerShell synchronization; "unified app management" "permissions". Read uam-tac-mac, manage-apps and MC796790: the change concerns availability, status, org-wide settings and installation.

claims.claim: The unified-management page describes no approval step for each synchronised change.
claims.quote: Searched: "unified app management" data permissions approval PowerShell synchronization; "unified app management" "permissions". Read uam-tac-mac in full: final migration requires consent, while later changes synchronise automatically.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: App availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.claim: The cited unified-management and Teams app-management pages do not name a licence for unification.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management Teams Microsoft 365 admin center licensing license requirements price meter. Read uam-tac-mac and manage-apps in full: neither states a licence for unification; manage-apps names an administrator role.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model for this app and agent management capability is unknown because Microsoft has not published an entitlement statement.
claims.quote: Before you can manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center, confirm the following requirements are met: Your organization has the required subscription and licenses for either Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, or Microsoft Agent 365.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and the first two sentences of Cost and licensing with: 'For agent management in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft requires the organisation to have the required subscription and licences for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot or Microsoft Agent 365, and appropriate licences for users who create, publish or use agents. A separate licence or meter for unification itself is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-365-overview. In the licensing Open question and cost rationale, replace the broad claim that licensing is unpublished with the narrower statement that a separate licence or meter for unification itself is not yet published.

claims.claim: No meter for unification itself is published in the documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management Teams Microsoft 365 admin center licensing license requirements price meter. Read uam-tac-mac, manage-apps, Teams service description and agent-365-overview; none publishes a unification meter.

claims.claim: Individual third-party apps can have separate publisher subscriptions or fees.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.

claims.claim: Administrators can export the app catalogue from the Teams admin center to review status and availability.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center. It can help you to coordinate with admin and security teams to evaluate agents and apps, verify availability, verify status, and more.

claims.claim: The unification path is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Move to unified app management.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for the unification step itself is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management move tenant unification PowerShell Microsoft Graph API TAC MAC; "unified" "app management" "PowerShell" migration; "unified app management" "API". Read uam-tac-mac and Update-M365TeamsApp: only UI migration is documented.

claims.claim: Allowing or blocking an app is at Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams command Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -IsBlocked $true sets an app's state.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: The availability path runs through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group IDs> updates group availability.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: App availability cannot be updated in bulk in the Teams admin center but can be through PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Custom apps switch is at Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Custom apps > Let users install and use available apps by default.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. ... Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp -isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled $True enables the org-wide Custom Apps switch for uploading and making custom apps available.
claims.quote: If the isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled is set to true, the switch is enabled. So that the custom apps can be uploaded as app packages and available in the organization's app store, vice versa.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp covers the Custom apps switch, not the Microsoft apps or Third-party apps switches.
claims.quote: There is a switch for managing Custom Apps in the Org-wide App Settings page of Teams Admin Center. The command can set the value of this switch.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center availability path is Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install.
claims.quote: Scroll down and select Edit Users or select the Users tab in the overview pane. ... Specific users/group in the organization can install means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app on their own from the store and use it in the client.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented specifically for the Microsoft 365 admin center's cross-application availability control.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Integrated apps cross application app availability users groups Microsoft Graph PowerShell API; "Integrated apps" "availability" "Microsoft Graph". Read cross-application app guide and Update-M365TeamsApp; no MAC-side operation is specified.

claims.claim: The cross-application app guide says its Integrated apps controls are available only to Global Admins.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins. Check your credentials before you proceed.

claims.claim: The cmdlet documentation does not explain how each Teams PowerShell call appears in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: "Update-M365TeamsApp" "Microsoft 365 admin center". Read Update-M365TeamsApp, Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp and uam-tac-mac; the references describe Teams settings without specifying MAC-side display of each call.

claims.claim: The cited cross-application app guide does not explain how its Global Admin requirement interacts with Teams Administrator permissions after unification.
claims.quote: Searched: "unified app management" "permissions". Read cross-application app guide, uam-tac-mac and manage-apps: the first requires Global Admin, while the latter pages describe Teams roles without reconciling MAC permissions.

claims.claim: Teams apps can be enhanced to work in Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app.
claims.quote: App developers can enhance their Microsoft Teams apps to work in Outlook and in Microsoft 365 App (formerly known as Office.com).
